lessons.title: Our work and the environment
lessons.html:
What is the environment?

The environment is everything around us: the soil, the water in the river and the borehole, the air, the veld, the trees, the birds and the animals. People are part of it too. On a farm or at a silo, the work we do every day can help or harm the environment.

How grain work can harm the environment

  • Dust: grain dust from loading and cleaning goes into the air. People breathe it in and it can cause chest problems.
  • Chemicals: insect poisons, fumigants, diesel and oil can poison soil and water if they spill.
  • Waste: plastic, bags, oil cans and spoiled grain left lying around pollute the land and attract rats.
  • Noise: dryers, fans and trucks can be loud for workers and neighbours.
  • Water: washing equipment can carry dirt and chemicals into a stream.

Why it matters

We all need clean water to drink and clean air to breathe. Cattle drink from the dam. Crops grow in the soil. If we poison the soil or water, we harm our own families, our animals and our food. South Africa also has laws that protect water, such as the National Water Act 36 of 1998. A farm that pollutes can be fined.

Look around you

Take a walk around your work area. Look for:

  • oil drips under a tractor or truck,
  • bags and plastic blowing in the wind,
  • spilled grain near the intake pit,
  • empty chemical containers left outside,
  • taps that are left running.

Each of these is a small problem that can become a big one. Seeing it is the first step to fixing it.

lessons.title: Handling waste, spills and resources
lessons.html:
Waste goes in the right place

Every farm should have a place for each kind of waste. Learn where each one goes.

WasteWhere it goes
Paper, plastic, bagsGeneral waste or recycling bin
Spoiled grain and sweepingsScreenings bin or the place your supervisor shows you
Used oil and diesel ragsClosed oil drum, kept on a drip tray
Empty chemical containersLocked chemical store, for safe disposal. Never reuse.

Never do this

  • Never burn plastic, tyres or chemical containers.
  • Never use an empty poison container to carry water or food.
  • Never pour oil, diesel or chemicals into the soil, a drain or a river.
  • Never bury chemical waste on the farm.

When something spills

  1. Keep people and animals away.
  2. If it is a chemical, do not touch it without the right gloves and mask.
  3. Stop the spill if you can do it safely, for example close the tap of the drum.
  4. Cover the spill with sand or absorbent material so it does not spread.
  5. Tell your supervisor at once.

Save water and power

Water and electricity cost money and are scarce in many parts of South Africa. Close taps when you finish. Report leaking pipes. Switch off lights, fans and machines that are not needed, but only if you are allowed to switch them off. Sweep dry before you wash, so you use less water.

Keep dust down

Wear your dust mask. Close covers on conveyors. Do not blow dust with compressed air. Sweep gently so dust does not fly up.

lessons.title: Reporting and caring every day
lessons.html:
You are the eyes on the ground

Managers cannot see everything. Workers walk the site every day. You are often the first to see a problem. When you report it early, it is small and cheap to fix.

What to report

  • A spill of oil, diesel or chemical.
  • Dead birds, fish or animals near the silo or dam. They may be poisoned.
  • Smoke or a strange smell.
  • Water that changes colour or smells bad.
  • Rats, pigeons or insects in large numbers.
  • Broken bins or waste that is blowing away.

How to report

Tell your supervisor. Say clearly:

  1. What you saw.
  2. Where it is.
  3. When you saw it.
  4. What you already did, for example "I put sand on the oil."

Your supervisor may write it in an incident book or report form.

Protect the veld and animals

Many farms have veld, wetlands and wild animals. Drive only on the roads, so you do not damage the grass. Do not light fires in the veld. Do not catch or hurt wild animals. Owls and snakes catch rats, so they help the farm.

Good habits

Being environment aware is a habit. Pick up rubbish when you see it. Put the lid back on the bin. Tell new workers where the waste goes. Small things done by everyone make a big difference.

Key points

  • Our work with dust, chemicals, waste and water can harm the environment.
  • Put each kind of waste in the right place and never burn or bury chemical waste.
  • Never reuse an empty chemical container.
  • For a spill: keep people away, contain it with sand and report it.
  • Report what, where and when to your supervisor.
